rationale: Re-execute the transfer experiment with the harness ordering corrected: the target's own configuration view is read after DemoteVoter returns and polled until it shows the new role, so the recorded role describes the moment the transfer is requested. The same four comparisons are retained so the outcomes remain comparable with the earlier receipts.

scope.description: The same two leadership-transfer cases on real four-voter in-memory clusters: the trigger demotes a non-leader member before LeadershipTransferToServer names it, the control leaves it a voter. After the demotion the harness polls the demoted member's own GetConfiguration until its role changes, records how long that took, and only then requests the transfer, so the case event's role value and the per-sample candidate/leaderless counts describe the state at transfer time.
assumptions: All members run the captured code on the in-memory transport with inmemConfig timeouts (Heartbeat/Election/Lease 50 ms).

The demotion poll waits up to 3 s for the target's own configuration view to report the new role; a case that never converges is recorded with demotion_converged=false and the transfer proceeds anyway.
A leaderless sample means no member reported Leader at that instant, sampled about every 10 ms over roughly 4.7 s.
Both cases run in one execution; each builds and closes its own cluster.
excluded: No claim about client requests during the window and no safety claim about committed entries.
Transfers to members absent from the configuration entirely remain unexercised.

parameters.trigger_target: member demoted to non-voter before the transfer, after its own view converges

experiment.prefix: Each case calls MakeClusterCustom with four bootstrapped voters, waits for c.Leader(), selects the first non-leader raft as target, and records roleBefore from the target's own GetConfiguration. The trigger then calls leader.DemoteVoter(targetID, 0, 5s) and polls the target's own configuration every 10 ms for up to 3 s until it reports nonvoter, recording demotion_converged and demotion_converge_ms; the control skips demotion. Both then read the target's role again as target_role_in_own_config, emit the case event, call leader.LeadershipTransferToServer(targetID, target.localAddr), record the future outcome, and sample target.State() and every member's State() every 10 ms for five seconds.
semantic_changes: target_role_in_own_config now answers what the target believed when the transfer was requested, which the earlier receipts could not establish.
A case additionally records whether the demoted member ever observed its new role and how long that took.
experiment.responsibility: The library owns target eligibility: it holds the latest configuration, its automatic path already excludes non-voters, and its documentation states that a follower which cannot be promoted will fail gracefully. A caller naming a configured member relies on the library either to refuse an ineligible target or to report an outcome matching what happened to authority.

comparisons.description: Control: a transfer to a voter must install that voter as leader.
Control: a transfer that installs the named voter must complete without error.
A transfer to a member whose own configuration view now says non-voter cannot be promoted, so the documented graceful failure requires an error.
If the transfer is admitted as successful, the named target must hold leadership.

experiment.revision_reason: The target's suffrage view is now read after DemoteVoter returns and polled every 10 ms until it reports the new role, instead of being read before the demotion. Case events add target_role_before, demotion_converged and demotion_converge_ms; case names, admissions and assertions are unchanged.
